articles.abstract: The present paper is the first in a series regarding the deformed Hermitian-Yang-Mills equation. The goal is to discuss a mirror symmetry related to a geometric duality. Much of the work concerns an associated infinite dimensional symplectic manifold for which the geodesics and approximate geodesics are investigated. The geodesic structure of the space of Kähler metrics is also studied.

articles.title: On tau-functions for the KdV hierarchy
articles.abstract: For an arbitrary solution to the Korteweg-de Vries (KdV) hierarchy, the generating series of logarithmic derivatives of the tau-function of the solution can be expressed by the basic matrix resolvent via algebraic manipulations. Based on this the authors develop in this paper two new formulae for the generating series by introducing a pair of wave functions of the solution. Applications to the Witten-Kontsevich tau-function, to the generalized Brézin-Gross-Witten (BGW) tau-function, as well as to a modular deformation of the generalized BGW tau-function which they call the Lamé tau-function are also given. The paper is organized as follows. Section 1, is an introduction to the subject. Here, the authors recall the definitions of all of the main objects studied (KdV hierarchy, tau-function, matrix resolvents, wave functions,...), in some cases with definitions slightly different from the most standard ones. In Section 2, the authors review the MR approach. In Sections 3 and 4, they prove the main results and compute explicitly some generalized BGW correlators. In Section 5, they compute Lamé correlators and further remarks are given in Section 6.

articles.title: The Kirby torus trick for surfaces
articles.abstract: Summary: The classical theorem that topological surfaces can be triangulated is proved using the torus trick of Kirby plus a few basic facts about smooth or PL surfaces.

articles.title: The KW equations and the Nahm pole boundary condition with knots
articles.abstract:
In this detailed technical paper the authors extend further their previous analysis of the Kapustin-Witten (KW) equations with Nahm pole boundary condition now adapted to general 4-manifolds-with-boundary such that the boundary-3-manifold contains a knot or more generally a link.

The motivation is a conjecture of the second author that the coefficients of the Laurent expansion of the Jones polynomial of a link \(L\subset {\mathbb R}^3\) arise by counting solutions of the KW equations on the half-space \({\mathbb R}^4_+\) obeying a generalized Nahm pole boundary condition on \(\partial {\mathbb R}^4_+={\mathbb R}^3\supset L\) i.e. the Nahm pole boundary condition generalized to be compatible with the extra information of containing a link on the boundary. Roughly this means to prescribe further singularities in the Higgs field part of the KW pair along each link component while the connection part is continuous up to the boundary as before. The conjecture is important because it is well-known that computing the Jones polynomial of a link is an exponentially difficult problem in terms of e.g. the crossing number of any plane diagram of the link.

articles.title: A Teichmüller space for negatively curved surfaces
articles.abstract:
Let \(\Sigma\) be a closed surface of genus at least two. The Teichmüller space of \(\Sigma\), i.e., the moduli space of hyperbolic metrics up to diffeomorphisms isotopic to the identity, is homeomorphic to \(\mathbb{R}^{6g-6}\). It has an interpretation as a connected component of the space \[\mathrm{Hom}(\pi_1(\Sigma),\mathrm{SL}(2,\mathbb R))/\mathrm{SL}(2,\mathbb R)\] of (reductive) representations of the fundamental group of \(\Sigma\) into \(\mathrm{SL}(2,\mathbb R)\) up to conjugation. Equivalently, \(\mathrm{Hom}(\pi_1(\Sigma),\mathrm{SL}(2,\mathbb R))/\mathrm{SL}(2,\mathbb R)\) may be viewed as the moduli space of reductive flat \(\mathrm{SL}(2,\mathbb{R})\)-connections on \(\Sigma\).

In [Topology 31, No. 3, 449--473 (1992; Zbl 0769.32008)] the author has shown, that for \(n\geq 2\) the embedding \(\mathrm{SL}(2,\mathbb{R})\subset \mathrm{SL}(n,\mathbb{R})\) given by the irreducible \(n\)-dimensional representation of \(\mathrm{SL}(2,\mathbb{R})\) induces an embedding of the Teichmüller space into a distinguished connected component of \(\mathrm{Hom}(\pi_1(\Sigma),\mathrm{SL}(n,\mathbb{R}))/\mathrm{SL}(n,\mathbb{R})\), the so-called Hitchin component. The proof fixes a complex structure on \(\Sigma\) and uses the theory of \(\mathrm{SL}(n,\mathbb{C})\)-Higgs bundles to realize the Hitchin component as a section of the Hitchin map, which is a holomorphic map from the moduli space of (polystable) Higgs bundles to the vector space \(\bigoplus_{m=2}^n H^0(\Sigma,K^m)\), the so-called Hitchin base.

Recall that an \(\mathrm{SL}(n,\mathbb{C})\)-Higgs bundle is a pair \((E,\Phi)\) consisting of a holomorphic vector bundle \(E\) over \(\Sigma\) with trivial determinant and a trace-free holomorphic section \(\Phi\in H^0(\mathrm{End}(E)\otimes K)\), the Higgs field. The link between Higgs bundles and flat connections is provided by the non-abelian Hodge correspondence which ensures the existence of a hermitian metric on a polystable Higgs bundle \((E,\Phi)\), such that the \(\mathrm{SU}(n)\)-self-duality equations \[F^\nabla + [\Phi,\Phi^*] =0,\qquad \overline\partial\Phi=0,\] hold, where \(\nabla\) is the associated Chern connection. These equations imply that the \(\mathrm{SL}(n,\mathbb{C})\)-connection \(\nabla+\Phi+\Phi^*\) is flat. To obtain a flat \(\mathrm{SL}(n,\mathbb{R})\)-connection one requires a reduction of the structure group of \(E\) to \(\mathrm{SO}(n,\mathbb{C})\), i.e., a holomorphic orthogonal structure, and \(\Phi\) to take values in the symmetric endomorphisms of \(E\). Conversely, starting from a flat \(\mathrm{SL}(n,\mathbb{R})\)-connection \(D\), Corlette's theorem produces a harmonic section of the associated \(\mathrm{SL}(n,\mathbb{R})/\mathrm{SO}(n)\)-bundle, so that \(D\) can be written in the form \(D = \nabla+\Phi+\Phi^*\) for a solution \((\nabla,\Phi)\) of the self-duality equations as above.

Since the classical Teichmüller space may be viewed as the moduli space of hyperbolic Riemannian metrics on \(\Sigma\) (up to diffeomorphisms isotopic to the identity), it is a natural problem to find geometric structures on \(\Sigma\) whose moduli spaces are parametrised by Hitchin components.

In this paper, further developing his recent work [Surv. Differ. Geom. 21, 139--163 (2016; Zbl 1391.53061)], the author studies this question in the case of \(\mathrm{SL}(\infty,\mathbb{R})\), which is viewed here as the group of Hamiltonian diffeomorphisms of \(T^*S^1 \cong S^1\times \mathbb{R}\). The starting point of the paper is the observation that for a negatively curved Riemannian metric on \(\Sigma\) the space of oriented geodesics on the universal cover \(\widetilde\Sigma\) is the symplectic manifold \(S^1\times\mathbb{R}\) and the fundamental group \(\pi_1(\Sigma)\) acts naturally by Hamiltonian diffeomorphisms. Thus, there is a natural representation \(\pi_1(\Sigma)\to \mathrm{SL}(\infty,\mathbb{R})\) associated with a negatively curved metric on \(\Sigma\).

In Section 3, starting from a negatively curved metric on \(\Sigma\), the author gives a natural geometric construction of a flat symplectic connection on a symplectic \(S^1\times \mathbb{R}\)-bundle over \(\Sigma\) whose holonomy gives the representation described above. Since the holonomy of this connection lies in the proper subgroup \(\mathrm{Sp}(\infty,\mathbb{R})\) of Hamiltonian diffeomorphisms commuting with the involution given by reversing the orientation of an oriented geodesic, this construction is then generalised in Section 4 to negatively curved Finsler metrics on \(\Sigma\). Motivated by the aim to obtain a moduli space of such connections playing the role of the Hitchin component in this setting, the author then considers in \S 5 deformations of the symplectic connection associated with a hyperbolic metric. In particular, he describes a family of first order deformations parametrised by the vector space of CR-functions on the unit circle bundle of \(\Sigma\). This vector space contains in particular the space \(H^0(\Sigma,K^m)\) for \(m\geq 2\) in a natural way and the author suggests that this space of CR-functions should play the role of the Hitchin base \(\bigoplus_{m=2}^nH^0(\Sigma,K^m)\) in the \(\mathrm{SL}(\infty,\mathbb{R})\)-setting.

Since the group \(\mathrm{SL}(\infty,\mathbb{R})\) does not have a natural complexification, the link to the Higgs bundle approach to flat connections does not generalise in an obvious way from the \(\mathrm{SL}(n,\mathbb{R})\) case with finite \(n\) to the \(\mathrm{SL}(\infty,\mathbb{R})\) situation. The final section Section 6 explains the framework of \(\mathrm{SL}(\infty,\mathbb{R})\) Higgs bundles and provides a conjectural picture of how the symplectic connection above may be obtained from an appropriate solution to the \(\mathrm{SU}(\infty)\)-self-duality equations. From [the author, Surv. Differ. Geom. 21, 139--163 (2016; Zbl 1391.53061)], it is known that such a solution of the \(\mathrm{SU}(\infty)\)-self-duality equations is given by a hyper-Kähler metric on a symplectic \(S^2\)-bundle over \(\Sigma\) with a fold singularity on the equator of each \(S^2\)-fibre. This singular set is a circle bundle over \(\Sigma\) and should be the unit circle bundle for a Finsler metric on \(\Sigma\). \textit{O. Biquard} [Bull. Soc. Math. Fr. 147, No. 2, 303--340 (2019; Zbl 1432.53069)] has shown that there is a family of folded hyper-Kähler structures deforming the folded hyper-Kähler structure associated with a hyperbolic metric parametrised by a neighbourhood of the origin in the space \(\bigoplus_{m\geq 2}H^0(\Sigma,K^m)\).

Such a folded hyper-Kähler structure admits an analytic continuation as a (folded) hypersymplectic structure to a neighbourhood of the unit circle bundle and the author explains that there is a natural flat symplectic connection associated with such a hypersymplectic structure. He considers in detail deformations by sections of \(H^0(\Sigma,K^2)\) and shows that in this case there exists a global folded hypersymplectic structure whose associated symplectic connection is equivalent to the one constructed in the first part of the paper.

articles.title: Complément to the Thurston 3D-geometrization picture
articles.abstract:
By the geometrization of 3-manifolds, closed oriented prime 3-manifolds can be decomposed into ``elementary primes'' which are quotients by discrete subgroups of isometries of one of the eight Thurston homogeneous Riemannian geometries (both three of hyperbolic type and of affinely flat type, two of elliptic type), called ``compound primes'' by the authors in case of a nontrivial decomposition. ``The point of the paper is to construct these compound primes \textit{geometrically} using the six Lie groups corresponding to the six geometries of hyperbolic or affine type. Thus, we build specific \textit{Lie generated geometries} on all of the compound prime closed oriented three-manifolds.'' The main theorem of the paper, in part written in the style of a (historical) essay on 3-manifolds and their geometries, is the following.

``Excepting those covered by \(S^3\) and \(S^2 \times\mathbb{R}\), every closed oriented prime 3-manifold has a canonical non-empty finite dimensional moduli space of Lie generated geometries defined by four Lie groups of dimensions (6,6,4,4) acting on the upper half space.''

As the authors note, this solves, using geometrization, a 45-year-old question/approach to the Poincaré conjecture as documented in a paper by \textit{D. Sullivan} and \textit{W. Thurston} [Enseign. Math. (2) 29, 15--25 (1983; Zbl 0529.53025)].

Knots, perturbative series and quantum modularity
articles.abstract:
This is a companion paper of [\textit{S. Garoufalidis} and \textit{D. Zagier}, SIGMA, Symmetry Integrability Geom. Methods Appl. 19, Paper 082, 39 p. (2023; Zbl 1532.57004)]. Based on the volume conjecture, the refined quantum modularity conjecture is studied. In this article, the authors introduce a matrix-valued invariant \(\mathbf{J}^{(K)}(X)\) as a generalization of the Kashaev invariant of a knot \(K\). The invariant \(\mathbf{J}^{(K)}\) is indexed either in terms of boundary parabolic representations of the fundamental group of \(S^3\setminus K\) or flat connections. They propose the refined quantum modularity conjecture, which states that for \(\gamma\in SL_2(\mathbf{Z})\) the invariant \(\mathbf{J}^{(K)} (\gamma X)\) with \(X\in \mathbb{Q}\) tending to infinity behaves
\[
\mathbf{J}^{(K)}(\gamma X) \approx \widetilde{\mathbf{j}}_\gamma(X) \mathbf{J}^{(K)}(X) \widehat{\boldsymbol{\Phi}}^{(K)}_{a/c} \left( \frac{2\pi \mathrm{i}}{c(cX+d)} \right),
\]
where \(\widetilde{\mathbf{j}}_\gamma(X)\) is a diagonal automorphy factor, and \(\widehat{\boldsymbol{\Phi}}^{(K)}_\alpha(h)\) denotes a power series. Also conjectured is that the cocycle
\[
W_\gamma(x)= \mathbf{J}(\gamma x)^{-1} \widetilde{\mathbf{j}}_\gamma(x) \mathbf{J}(x)
\]
is a \(C^\infty\) function on \(\mathbb{R}\setminus \{\gamma^{-1}(\infty)\}\). These are discovered based on numerical computations for \(K\) being \(4_1\), \(5_2\), and \((-2,3,7)\)-pretzel. Evidence for these conjectures and other interesting properties is given.
